heroHeadline: Day 13 of MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Closure; UN Issues Formal Displacement Warning — 30,000+ Displaced; ACLED: Record 38 Deaths in Sud-Est as Gang 'Balloon Effect' Spreads Violence to New Departments; GBV Surges 43%
heroSubtitle: JURIST on May 22 reported a formal UN warning on surging mass displacement in Haiti, as the violence wave that erupted on May 10 in Cité Soleil and the Cul-de-Sac Plain entered its 13th consecutive day. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only emergency facility for ~300,000 commune residents — remains closed with no announced reopening timeline. ACLED's May 2026 overview documented a record 38 deaths in the historically low-violence Sud-Est department (including Macary and Seguin), with analysts warning of a 'balloon effect' as GSF/HNP pressure in Port-au-Prince displaces gang factions to regions with no international security presence. The GSF's ~800-person advance force (400+ Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) remains exclusively concentrated in Port-au-Prince's city center; Artibonite, Centre, and Sud-Est have zero GSF coverage. PassBlue (May 21) reported UN data documenting approximately 21 GBV cases per day in Q1 2026 — a 43% increase from Q4 2025, with 70%+ involving rape. Total displacement has reached ~1.5 million. PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 declaration that August 30 elections are 'impossible' stands unrevised; no electoral decree issued; voter registration has not begun; 23 communes inaccessible. The 2026 HRP is only ~20% funded ($172M of $880M). Approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders in the US await the Supreme Court's ruling in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — expected late June 2026.
